solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Inspectors' appraisal fools people, in a way

parts.note: fools are asses, plural noun to plural noun

indicators.note: in says the word for people sits inside the abbreviation for a way

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
people are men in the old general sense

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses an inspectors' report as making fools of people in some fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: An assessment is the formal judgement or evaluation that inspectors produce after a visit.

clue.text: Seen in church when spring is over before Easter starts

indicators.note: is over, in a down clue, tells us the word for spring is turned upside down

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring

indicators.note: starts asks for the opening letter of the word Easter

explanation.surface: A churchgoer notes that something appears once spring has passed, just ahead of Easter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is over' turns SPA into APS; 'starts' takes E from Easter. 'spring' looks like the season beside Easter, but it is a source of water.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is the vaulted recess at the east end of a church, so it is something seen in one.

clue.text: It's the gap formed at the M6 No.6 Junction

indicators.note: formed says the letters of these three words are shaped into something new

explanation.surface: A motorist points to the gap left in the road at a famous motorway interchange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'formed' rearranges ITS THE GAP. Junction 6 of the M6 near Birmingham is the tangled interchange nicknamed Spaghetti Junction.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gravelly Hill Interchange at M6 junction 6 is popularly called Spaghetti Junction, so the first word of its nickname stands for it.

clue.text: It's an odd sort of stuff

indicators.note: odd sort of says these letters are made into an unusual version of themselves

explanation.surface: Someone looks at a strange material and calls it a peculiar kind of stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd sort of' rearranges ITSAN. 'stuff' is the old word for woven cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuff is an old name for fabric, and satin is a glossy woven fabric.

clue.text: Arrange a star part in a Western

definitions.meaning: to arrange is to put people or things in order, as troops are drawn up

definitions.text: a star part in a Western
definitions.meaning: the lawman with the badge is a leading role in many cowboy films

explanation.surface: A director organises a leading role in a cowboy film.
explanation.definitionFit: To marshal is to arrange in order, and a US marshal is a classic lead character in Westerns.

clue.text: What the poor man has and the rich man wants

definitions.text: What the poor man has and the rich man wants

parts.words: What the poor man has and the rich man wants
parts.note: a riddle: read as a lack, the poor possess an absence of things, and the rich man, having everything, lacks only that absence

explanation.surface: A proverb-like riddle contrasting the poor and the wealthy.
explanation.definitionFit: The poor have no possessions, and someone who has everything wants for nothing more, so emptiness answers both halves.

clue.text: Young bird lacking the knowledge to be fashionable

indicators.note: lacking says the word for knowledge is removed from the bird

parts.note: a chicken is a young fowl
ken is knowledge, as in beyond one's ken

explanation.surface: A naive youngster tries to be stylish without any real know-how.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' removes KEN from CHICKEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Chic means stylish and elegant, a direct synonym of fashionable.

clue.text: Uplift one gets in a crowd

indicators.note: gets in says the numeral for one enters the word for a crowd

parts.note: a host is a great crowd, as in a host of angels
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone gains a lift of spirits by joining a throng.
explanation.definitionFit: To hoist is to raise or lift up, so it matches uplift as a verb.

clue.text: I'd turn up to break agreement in dispute

indicators.note: to break says the reversed piece splits the word for an agreement

parts.note: a contract is a binding agreement

indicators.note: turn up, in a down clue, reads the letters of I'd from the bottom

explanation.surface: Someone arrives to wreck a deal that is under dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn up' makes DI, which 'to break' places inside CONTRACT: CONTRA-DI-CT.
explanation.definitionFit: To contradict is to dispute what someone has said by asserting the opposite.

clue.text: Appeal for admittance when about to dine

indicators.note: about says the word for admittance wraps around the word for dine

parts.note: entry means admittance, being let in
to dine is to eat

explanation.surface: A hungry guest begs to be let in just as dinner is about to be served.
explanation.definitionFit: An entreaty is an earnest plea or appeal.

clue.text: Quick trim

definitions.meaning: quick in the sense of brisk
trim in the sense of neat and well turned out

explanation.surface: A barber offers a fast haircut.
explanation.definitionFit: Smart can mean brisk and fast, as in a smart pace, and also neat and tidy in appearance.

clue.text: Enter into an arrangement for storage

indicators.note: an arrangement says the letters of the two words are set in a new order

explanation.surface: A business enters into a deal for warehouse space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'an arrangement' rearranges ENTERINTO; 'for' links it to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Retention is the keeping or holding of something, as in data retention, which is storage.

clue.text: A city to impress sailors

definitions.meaning: a great port city in China
to impress is to force into naval service, as press gangs did to sailors

explanation.surface: A city that impresses seafarers with its sights.
explanation.definitionFit: Shanghai is China's largest city, and to shanghai is to kidnap men to serve as sailors.

clue.text: Chopper blade going to and fro

indicators.note: going to and fro says the word reads the same in either direction

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A helicopter blade whirls back and forth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going to and fro' points to a palindrome, and also pictures the spinning blade.
explanation.definitionFit: The rotor is the rotating assembly of blades that lifts a helicopter, slang chopper.

clue.text: Edits a clue, perhaps — makes it clear

indicators.note: perhaps suggests these letters may be arranged differently

explanation.surface: An editor tidies up a crossword clue so it reads clearly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges EDITSACLUE.
explanation.definitionFit: To elucidate is to explain and make plain, so elucidates means makes something clear.

clue.text: Fired with real reform and no exaggeration?

parts.note: lit means fired, as a fire or fuse is set going

indicators.note: reform says the letters of real are formed again in another order

explanation.surface: Someone fired up with zeal for genuine reform insists they are not exaggerating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reform' rearranges REAL into ERAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Literal means taking words in their exact sense, free of embellishment or overstatement.

clue.text: Marathon, say, around New York, running last, not yet set for breakfast

indicators.note: around says the race and the example abbreviation sit either side of the city

parts.note: a marathon is a long run
say means for example, abbreviated EG

indicators.note: last asks for the final letter of the word running

explanation.surface: A marathon around New York is run, with a runner trailing in last.
explanation.walkthrough: RUN and EG go 'around' NY to give RUNNYEG; 'last' adds G from running.
explanation.definitionFit: A runny egg is a soft-boiled or fried egg whose yolk has not set, a breakfast favourite.

clue.text: Excellent publicity arranged by one of the family

parts.note: grand means excellent, as in a grand day out
an ad is publicity for a product

explanation.surface: A relative arranges some fine publicity.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandad is a grandfather, a family member.

clue.text: Cause of outburst as school roster is put up after first of December

indicators.note: first of asks for the opening letter of the word December

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school

indicators.note: is put up, in a down clue, reads the word for roster upwards

parts.note: a rota is a roster of duties

explanation.surface: A school timetable posted at the start of December causes an outcry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is put up' turns ROTA into ATOR. Eton College is an English boarding school near Windsor.
explanation.definitionFit: A detonator is the device that sets off an explosion, a literal outburst.

clue.text: Customers offer £1 in foreign money

indicators.note: in says the pound sign's letter goes inside the word for coins

parts.note: cents are coins of the US and euro area, foreign to a British setter
the pound sign is L, from Latin libra, and the figure 1 is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Shoppers offer a pound note when paying in a foreign currency.
explanation.definitionFit: Clients are customers who buy services from a professional or business.

clue.text: Weather forecast favourable — fear it's incorrect

indicators.note: incorrect says these letters appear in the wrong order and must be fixed

explanation.surface: A forecaster predicts fine weather, while a sceptic fears it is wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incorrect' rearranges FEARITS. Set fair is the barometer reading for settled weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Set fair describes weather that is settled and fine, a favourable forecast.

clue.text: Enigmatic, keen and in charge, set about exercising

indicators.note: set about says the first two pieces are placed around the third

parts.note: to keen is to wail, to cry in grief
PT is physical training, exercising

explanation.surface: A mysterious, eager boss starts a workout session.
explanation.walkthrough: CRY and IC are 'set about' PT: CRY-PT-IC. 'keen' looks like eager but is the verb to wail.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic means mysterious and hidden in meaning, as an enigma is.

clue.text: Linen chest that's new, look inside

indicators.note: inside says the word for look goes within the rearranged chest
new asks for the letters of chest made into a fresh order

parts.note: lo is an old word for look, as in lo and behold

explanation.surface: Someone peers into a new chest full of linen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns CHEST into CTHES, and LO goes 'inside' after the C.
explanation.definitionFit: Linen can mean clothing, especially underclothes and shirts once made of linen.

clue.text: Lydia comes round regularly

indicators.note: comes round says the letters of the name are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: A friend called Lydia drops in on a routine basis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes round' rearranges LYDIA. The surface also hints at a daily, British slang for a cleaner who visits each day.
explanation.definitionFit: Daily as an adverb means every day, happening regularly.

clue.text: Not much land, in the main, but somebody's leased it

definitions.text: Not much land, in the main
definitions.meaning: the main is the sea, so this is a small piece of land surrounded by water
split into two words, it reads as a statement that it has been rented out

explanation.surface: A small island in the sea has been rented out by someone.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is a pun: split the answer as IS LET and it says the place has been leased.
explanation.definitionFit: An islet is a very small island in the sea, and is let means has been leased.

clue.text: A large number of free handouts

indicators.note: free says the letters of handouts are loosed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A lot of free handouts are being given away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' rearranges HANDOUTS.
explanation.definitionFit: A thousand is a big number, often used loosely to mean very many.

clue.text: Strength is rising afresh

indicators.note: rising, in a down clue, says the word is reads upwards

parts.note: afresh means anew, giving new

explanation.surface: Someone's strength is coming back again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns IS into SI.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinew means a tendon, and figuratively physical strength or power.

clue.text: Some poetry does need editing

indicators.note: need editing says the letters of does must be reworked into another order

explanation.surface: A critic remarks that some verse really needs revising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'need editing' rearranges DOES.
explanation.definitionFit: Odes are lyric poems, so a set of them is some poetry.

clue.text: Great help at sea in rapid communication

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A ship in distress gets great help from a fast message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges GREATHELP. The answer is also the newspaper's own name.
explanation.definitionFit: The telegraph was the fastest long-distance messaging system of the nineteenth century.

clue.text: Observed college is backed by deputy head

indicators.note: is backed says the word for the college is read backwards

parts.note: Eton College is the famous English school

indicators.note: head asks for the first letter of the word deputy

explanation.surface: Someone notices that a college has the support of the deputy headteacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is backed' turns ETON into NOTE; 'head' gives D from deputy. 'deputy head' looks like one school post.
explanation.definitionFit: Noted means noticed or observed, as in she noted the time.

clue.text: Place it within the borders of Singapore

indicators.note: within says the word it sits inside the outer letters
the borders of asks for the first and last letters of Singapore

explanation.surface: Someone is told to put it inside Singapore's frontiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the borders of' gives S and E from Singapore, and 'within' puts IT between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A site is a location or place, as in a building site.

clue.text: Angry expressions which call for solutions

definitions.meaning: split in two, angry words exchanged in a quarrel
puzzles in a grid that the solver must answer

explanation.surface: Heated words that demand a resolution.
explanation.definitionFit: Cross words are angry remarks, and crosswords are puzzles that require solving.
